plan: Plan track T15 (Bot complete) and ADR-043 (Bot: devices, pairing, control and safety); the computer plugin and the job worker serve OpenVibe.Actor and the Codes job runner (tracks T14/T17)
release: v0.14.0, published 2026-10-25 as a GitHub release (a plugin's command carries the operator Bot's gate saw and the robot's turn_epoch; a command older than the newest turn halt never reaches a driver): binaries for linux amd64/arm64/armv7, darwin amd64/arm64 and windows amd64, the plugins tarball, install.sh and SHA256SUMS
runtime: go 1.24 (one static binary per platform); plugins in Python 3; an ESP32 Arduino library
deployment: none of its own: people install it on their machines and robots (curl -fsSL https://openvibe.bot/install | sh, or a release binary); it connects out to OpenVibe.Bot (wss://openvibe.bot/device) and pairs through OpenVibe.Bot or OpenVibe.Network. On 2026-10-22 production held 1 platform node with 4 pairings and 5 node principals on Network, and 3 robots with 5 devices on Bot.
features: pairing with a code approved on openvibe.bot (or through Network), one outbound WebSocket, no open ports
safety: deadlines, owner limits clamped before any driver, heartbeats and a deadman, a persisted e-stop and the local kill switch (openvibe-node stop)

plugins as separate processes (JSON lines): dryrun, adeept_adr036, cozmo, relay and ros2 (rclpy or rosbridge); the community LOOI driver's contract; signed community profiles (openvibe-node profile verify)

the computer plugin for OpenVibe.Actor: terminal, files, screen, input and its own browser, at the level the owner sets on the machine (observe, ask, trusted, full); approvals in the tray (Linux, Windows), a notification or openvibe-node approve
the live screen: the machine's screen on openvibe.bot for its owner only, up to 30 minutes
the job worker (--worker): sandboxed function, code and linux jobs, and the OpenVibe.Codes job runner
one-command install on a Raspberry Pi or other Linux robot (I2C, SPI, camera tools, kit detection)
system service on systemd, launchd and Windows (or a Windows sign-in start)
ESP32 library (OpenVibeNode): pairing, control link, drive and actuator commands, telemetry, heartbeat, deadman and e-stop
notYet: code signing and notarization for Windows and macOS (the release has SHA256SUMS only)
a tray on macOS (approvals there are a dialog with Deny as its default)
the computer plugin's browser on Windows
